key_insight: A two-level machine-learning framework can efficiently map the thermodynamic phase stability of complex hybrid perovskite alloys across composition and phase space.
engineering_relevance: The results identify where stable compositions are most likely, helping guide alloy design for more durable perovskite solar cells, especially by showing tighter stability limits for Sn-based systems.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials trained on DFT data perform fast structure relaxations.
Secondary ML models predict energies directly from unrelaxed alloy structures.
Free-energy landscapes are computed across compositions while accounting for disorder and FA molecular orientations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports free-energy landscape calculations across (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3, showing narrower stable regions for the Sn-based alloys and no stabilization near the middle of composition space.
watch_item: The approach depends on ML models trained on DFT data, so prediction quality may be sensitive to training coverage and transferability outside the sampled alloy space.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
